arxiv-1703-06282.title: Comparing the dark matter models, modified Newtonian dynamics and modified gravity in accounting for the galaxy rotation curves
arxiv-1703-06282.creator: Xin Li, Li Tang, Hai-Nan Lin
arxiv-1703-06282.description: Abstract We compare six models (including the baryonic model, two dark matter models, two modified Newtonian dynamics models and one modified gravity model) in accounting for the galaxy rotation curves. For the dark matter models, we assume NFW profile and core-modified profile for the dark halo, respectively.

arxiv-1808-07858.title: Performance of top-quark and 𝑾 \boldsymbol{W} -boson tagging with ATLAS in Run 2 of the LHC
arxiv-1808-07858.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1808-07858.description: Abstract The performance of identification algorithms (“taggers”) for hadronically decaying top quarks and W W bosons in p ​ p pp collisions at s \sqrt{s} = 13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider is presented.

arxiv-2107-01972.title: Polynomial growth and asymptotic dimension
arxiv-2107-01972.creator: Panos Papasoglu
arxiv-2107-01972.description: Abstract . Bonamy et al [ 4 ] showed that graphs of polynomial growth have finite asymptotic dimension. We refine their result showing that a graph of polynomial growth strictly less than n k + 1 n^{k+1} has asymptotic dimension at most k k .

arxiv-2204-10444.creator: Kevin D. Vallejo 1,∗ , Firoza Kabir 1,2 , Narayan Poudel 1 , Chris A. Marianetti 3 , David H. Hurley 1 , Paul J. Simmonds 4,5 , Cody A. Dennett 1 , and Krzysztof Gofryk 1,†
arxiv-2204-10444.description: Abstract Actinide-based compounds exhibit unique physics due to the presence of 5 f electrons, and serve in many cases as important technological materials. Targeted thin film synthesis of actinide materials has been successful in generating high-purity specimens in which to study individual physical phenomena.

arxiv-2208-04016.title: Solving the Online Assignment Problem with Machine Learned Advice CCS: Theory of computation Online algorithms CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Applied computing Operations research
arxiv-2208-04016.creator: Clarence Gabriel R. Kasilag, Pollux M. Rey, Jhoirene B. Clemente
arxiv-2208-04016.description: Abstract . The online assignment problem deals with assigning n elements of one set to another set which arrives sequentially on a one-to-one basis. This problem is also known as the online weighted bipartite matching which produces the smallest weight perfect matching possible.

arxiv-2210-08406.title: On the angular anisotropy of the randomly-averaged magnetic neutron scattering cross section of nanoparticles
arxiv-2210-08406.creator: Michael P. Adams, Evelyn Pratami-Sinaga, Andreas Michels
arxiv-2210-08406.description: Abstract We calculate the magnetic SANS cross section of dilute ensembles of uniformly magnetized and randomly-oriented Stoner-Wohlfarth particles using the Landau-Lifshitz equation. The focus of our study is on the angular anisotropy of the magnetic SANS signal as it can be seen on a two-dimensional position-sensitive detector. Depending on the symmetry of the magnetic anisotropy of the particles ( e.g.

arxiv-2304-03733.title: Variational Bayes latent class analysis for EHR-based phenotyping with large real-world data
arxiv-2304-03733.creator: Brian Buckley, Adrian O’Hagan, Marie Galligan
arxiv-2304-03733.description: Abstract Bayesian approaches to patient phenotyping in clinical observational studies have been limited by the computational challenges associated with applying the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach to real-world data. Approximate Bayesian inference via optimization of the variational evidence lower bound, variational Bayes (VB), has been successfully demonstrated for other applications.

arxiv-2307-04069.title: Spectrally Constrained Optimization
arxiv-2307-04069.creator: Casey Garner Gilad Lerman Shuzhong Zhang
arxiv-2307-04069.description: Abstract We investigate how to solve smooth matrix optimization problems with general linear inequality constraints on the eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix. We present solution methods to obtain exact global minima for linear objective functions, i.e., F ⁡ ( 𝑿 ) = ⟨ 𝑪 , 𝑿 ⟩ F(\bm{X})=\langle\bm{C},\bm{X}\rangle , and perform exact projections onto the eigenvalue constraint set.

arxiv-2311-16009.title: On Split-State Quantum Tamper Detection and Non-Malleability
arxiv-2311-16009.creator: Thiago Bergamaschi, Naresh Goud Boddu
arxiv-2311-16009.description: Abstract Tamper-detection codes (TDCs) and non-malleable codes (NMCs) are now fundamental objects at the intersection of cryptography and coding theory. Both of these primitives represent natural relaxations of error-correcting codes and offer related security guarantees in adversarial settings where error correction is impossible.

arxiv-2402-00603.title: Search for electroweak production of supersymmetric particles in final states with two τ \tau -leptons in s = 13 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=13\,\text{Te\kern-1.00006ptV} p ​ p pp collisions with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2402-00603.description: Abstract Three searches for the direct production of τ \tau -sleptons or charginos and neutralinos in final states with at least two hadronically decaying τ \tau -leptons are presented. For chargino and neutralino production, decays via intermediate τ \tau -sleptons or W W and h h bosons are considered.

arxiv-2412-01144.title: strong approximation for the intersection of two quadrics
arxiv-2412-01144.creator: Dasheng Wei, Jie Xu, Yi Zhu
arxiv-2412-01144.description: Abstract . We study strong approximation for the intersection of two affine quadrics. As its application, we prove the fibration method for weak approximation over number fields of rank four with nonsplit fibers split by quadratic extensions. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 14G05 (11D57, 14F22) 1.

arxiv-2503-08467.creator: Oana Balmau, Anne-Marie Kermarrec, Rafael Pires, André Loureiro Espírito Santo, Martijn de Vos, Milos Vujasinovic
arxiv-2503-08467.description: Abstract . Mixture of experts (MoE) models achieve state-of-the-art results in language modeling but suffer from inefficient hardware utilization due to imbalanced token routing and communication overhead. While prior work has focused on optimizing MoE training and decoder architectures, inference for encoder-based MoE models in a multi-GPU with expert parallelism setting remains underexplored.

arxiv-2506-14867.title: Dyon Loops and Abelian Instantons
arxiv-2506-14867.creator: Isabel Garcia Garcia, Marius Kongsore, and Ken Van Tilburg
arxiv-2506-14867.description: Abstract We construct Abelian gauge field configurations that carry non-zero instanton number. Each such “Abelian instanton” is generated by a closed magnetic worldline in four-dimensional Euclidean space, provided the Abelian gauge field has non-trivial winding along the closed worldline. The resulting field configuration corresponds to a Euclidean dyon loop featuring non-zero instanton number.

arxiv-2512-08353.title: A reconstructed discontinuous approximation for distributed elliptic control problems
arxiv-2512-08353.creator: Ruo Li, Haoyang Liu, Jun Yin
arxiv-2512-08353.description: Abstract . In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for the distributed elliptic optimal control problems. It is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation which admits arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element.

pmc-11460574.title: Loss of tyrosine 211 phosphorylation of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) enhances postnatal mammary gland development
pmc-11460574.creator: Yi-Chun Shen, You-Zhe Lin, Wan-Rong Wu, Pei-Le Lin, Chien-Ching Liao, Feng-Chi Chung, Chia-Yun Chen, Ching-Yu Weng, Shao-Chun Wang
pmc-11460574.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The intricately orchestrated progression of mammary tissue development involves the precise coordination of gland differentiation and cellular proliferation. Nevertheless, the understanding of the role and regulatory mechanisms governing the DNA replication machinery in mammary gland development remains limited. Given the essential role of DNA replication in the viability of living cells, any genetic disturbance to its replicative function, in any form, will impede organ development. This circumstance poses a technical challenge in elucidating the potential function of cell proliferation in mammary morphogenesis.

pmc-11647290.title: Identifying essential resource parameters for pandemic preparedness and response: an international Delphi study within the EU PANDEM-2 project
pmc-11647290.creator: Berend H H Beishuizen, Mart L Stein, Joeri S Buis, Alma Tostmann, Caroline Green, James Duggan, Máire A Connolly, Chantal P Rovers, Aura Timen
pmc-11647290.description: AbstractObjectiveThe COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the crucial role of healthcare and public health resource management, where scarcity impairs pandemic response resulting in increased disease transmission, delayed patient care and poorer health outcomes. In the EU PANDEM-2 project, we aimed to identify essential resource parameters for pandemic preparedness and response in the context of an emerging viral respiratory illness.

pmc-11671879.title: Use of a large-bore 088 intracranial access support catheter for delivery of large intracranial devices: case series with the TracStar LDP in 125 cases
pmc-11671879.creator: Jessica K Campos, David A Zarrin, Benjamen M Meyer, Muhammad Waqas Khan, Fahad J Laghari, Jonathan C Collard de Beaufort, Gizal Amin, Narlin B Beaty, Matthew T Bender, Shuichi Suzuki, Geoffrey P Colby, Li-Mei Lin, Alexander L Coon
pmc-11671879.description: BackgroundThe delivery of neuroendovascular devices requires a robust proximal access platform. This demand has previously been met with a 6Fr long sheath (8Fr guide) that is placed in the proximal internal carotid artery (ICA) or vertebral artery segments. We share our experience with the first 0.088 inch 8Fr guide catheter designed for direct intracranial access.

pmc-11687900.title: Multiple independent genetic code reassignments of the UAG stop codon in phyllopharyngean ciliates
pmc-11687900.creator: Jamie McGowan, Thomas A. Richards, Neil Hall, David Swarbreck, Laurent Duret, Eva H. Stukenbrock, Laurent Duret, Eva H. Stukenbrock, Laurent Duret, Eva H. Stukenbrock
pmc-11687900.description: The translation of nucleotide sequences into amino acid sequences, governed by the genetic code, is one of the most conserved features of molecular biology. The standard genetic code, which uses 61 sense codons to encode one of the 20 standard amino acids and 3 stop codons (UAA, UAG, and UGA) to terminate translation, is used by most extant organisms.

pmc-13202181.title: Can artificial intelligence bridge critical gaps in hypertension prediction and risk assessment in low- and middle-income countries? A scoping review
pmc-13202181.creator: David Sasu, Tsatsu Agbettor, Angela Owusu Ansah, William Annoh, Lecia Ackerson, Ayeyi Adjoa Domeyo Ohene-Adu, Roselyn Sackitey-Matey
pmc-13202181.description: ObjectiveAccording to the WHO, as of 2025, 1.4 billion adults between the ages 30–79 were living with hypertension, with approximately two-thirds of that number from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). By 2025, the number of individuals with hypertension is expected to have reached 1.5 billion, with sub-Saharan Africa alone projected to have 74.7 million cases.
